active.name: AI Infrastructure Build-Out — Mega-Cap Compute & Software
active.thesis: Institutional capital is concentrating into the AI compute stack — silicon (NVDA, INTC), infrastructure software (MSFT, PLTR), and the platform/ad layer monetizing inference (META, AAPL). With VIX at 15.88, bullish put/call, and SPY above 50SMA, the TRANSITIONAL regime is being expressed through quality mega-cap tech rather than broad risk-on, suggesting capital is rotating UP the quality curve rather than out.
active.evidence: XLK accel_ratio 1.715 and QQQ accel_ratio 3.323 (14d bull rate 3.3x the 60d baseline) show genuine fresh acceleration, not just persistence. Software-Infrastructure (1.992) and Consumer Electronics (2.246) are leading the doubling-up.

active.name: Natural Gas Reversal — Early Commodity Flip
active.thesis: Natural gas has flipped from ACCELERATING_BEARISH to bullish (+0.37%/day 14d) while crude oil and broader energy commodities (USO, BNO, DBC) are flipping the other way — a divergence that historically signals supply-side gas tightening (storage draw, weather, or LNG export demand) independent of macro oil weakness. Early-stage and contrarian to the broader commodity tape.
active.evidence: UNG is the ONLY commodity in the universe with a bearish-to-bullish flip; every other energy and ag commodity is rolling over. The asymmetry is the signal — but 60d base is still -9.96%, so this is an inflection trade, not a confirmed trend.

newsletter:
**[THE SPINE]** Dollar strength is the dominant force this week, and it's bleeding straight into the precious metals complex. DXY at 99.72 is up 2.1% over 21 days, sitting above both its 21d and 50d SMAs with RSI 62.6 — the ACTIVE DXY_METALS_TAG signal is firing, and the backtest says this inverse holds (corr=-0.45 sustained in 70% of rolling 24-month windows). Gold is down 9% in 21 days, Silver down 18%, and the Precious Metals theme has been formally faded with GLD/SLV/GDX/GDXJ all accelerating bearish. Everything else this week — the choppy SPY tape, the yield drift, the sector rotation — orbits this dollar bid.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The regime read is CHOPPY/TRANSITIONAL at 8/10 confidence, with SPY flat-to-down (-0.4% over 21d), VIX nudging up to 18.1 but still in healthy contango with VIX3M at 20.8, and breadth split (43.5% bullish vs 34.6% bearish across 480 names). Yields are grinding higher across the curve — 2Y at 3.63 with RSI 67.6, 5Y up 6% over 21 days, 10Y at 4.53 — and per our backtest, do not call a ceiling here: the 10Y ceiling signal DOESN'T HOLD (yield kept rising 53% of the time post-signal). Rising yields plus rising DXY is the textbook setup that's crushing metals and keeping equity beta on its back foot. Oil at 89.33 is down 7.5% with RSI 41 — treat as trend, not a mean-reversion setup; the WTI oversold signal has zero edge (-3.87% in backtest).

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** XLV is the clear leader at +7.9% over 21d and +5.2% vs 50SMA — defensive healthcare is absorbing the rotation as growth digests. XLK is +2.0% on the tape but +8.5% vs 50SMA with ACCELERATING_BULLISH trajectory, so tech leadership underneath is intact even as the headline number cools. Energy (+2.7%) and Financials (+2.1%) round out the green; QQQ (-1.0%) and SPY (-0.4%) are the laggards. Money is flowing INTO Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and an unmapped accelerator — no outflows or flips registered, which tells you this is rotation within risk-on, not risk-off.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The Semiconductors complex is flagged CEILING — 13 months hot, +258% gain, the largest run in 11 years of record — manage exits, not entries, on extended SOXX/SMH names. The fresher setups are in Software - Infrastructure (1 month hot, only +3%, well below the typical +18% run length) and Internet Content & Information (1 month hot, -5% — early innings of a heat spell that typically runs 6 months) — both ACCELERATING/HOLDING_BULLISH with trend UP. Drug Manufacturers - General at 10 months hot and +29% is also near-record extended — that's an XLV tailwind but a late-cycle one. Avoid the metals dip-buy reflex: Gold RSI 32 and Silver RSI 30 look oversold, but the DXY signal is ACTIVE and the trend is the trend. No coiled un-run candidates cleared the filter today.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** DXY 100.54 is the tripwire — a break above resistance extends the dollar trend and locks in further pain for GLD/SLV/GDX and pressure on multinationals; a failure back below the 21d SMA (~98.88 support zone) is the only thing that gives metals room to bounce, and even then, remember 88% of washout lows get retested within 60 days — don't call a bottom on the first green candle. Secondary watch: 10Y at 4.687 resistance — a break there pressures duration and growth multiples regardless of the dollar.
